name: Story Night: a family story circle on the TV
track: Fire TV (primary). Mini challenges: AWS Builder, Open Source.
pitch: A Vega OS app for one evening activity. Each phone in the room joins by scanning a QR code. One phone photographs an old print, and the photo fills the TV. The elder telling the story speaks into their own phone. Everyone else sends follow-up questions privately from their phones. The person holding the remote picks the next question with the D-pad. The session becomes a 'family episode' that keeps the teller's voice, adds captions and replays on the TV. When two tellers remember the same photo differently, the app records both versions with attribution and shows the conflict as a question for the family. The model never decides which version is right.
primary_user: Households where three to eight people of different generations share one living room: grandparents, parents and children. An adult child usually organizes. Indian joint families and visiting diaspora families are the first segment (assumption).
original_mechanism: (1) A question relay: questions are submitted privately on phones and released publicly by the D-pad host, so the elder never sees a wall of questions and the host controls pacing. (2) A multi-teller claim ledger: Nova Lite extracts claims about each photo as structured data (who, where, when, event) with the speaker attached. Conflicts are detected deterministically by comparing year and place fields across speakers. They are shown on the TV for the family to resolve and are never merged by the model. (3) Episode compiler: photo, audio segments, word-timed captions, chapter questions and a timeline, replayable offline on the TV.
removal_test: This is a partial weakness, flagged honestly. Without the TV, two people can get most of the value from Willow or StoryCorps on a phone. The TV is indispensable only for the group form: three or more people looking at one large photo together, a host who controls turn-taking from the couch, and replaying the archive at the next gathering. If falsification shows that families of three or more are as happy with a single phone, the concept fails.
wow_moment_45s: 0:00 Grandma taps 'Snap' on her phone and a 1978 print fills the TV within about 3 s. 0:05–0:25 She talks into her phone, and live caption text appears under the photo. 0:25 Two grandchildren's questions arrive as cards on the TV. The host presses D-pad right and OK on 'Who took this photo?'. 0:35 A 'Grandpa says 1979?' conflict chip appears beside the '1978 · Pune' chip on the timeline. 0:40 The TV replays the chapter in her own voice with word-synced captions.

mvp_scope: Vega app (RN 0.83, or 0.72 as fallback) running on the VVD with four screens: room lobby with QR, photo stage with a question queue, timeline view, and episode player
Phone PWA: join by QR, consent screen, photo capture, push-to-talk recording, question submission, delete my recordings
Realtime room: API Gateway WebSocket, Lambda and DynamoDB (presence, roles, events), with reconnect
Pipeline: upload to S3 through presigned URLs, then Amazon Transcribe batch with word timestamps, then Nova Lite structured output (three follow-up questions plus a claims JSON)
Deterministic conflict detection on year and place claims, with a conflict chip on the TV that only the family can resolve
Episode player: Ken Burns-style pan over the photo, the teller's audio, word-synced captions styled from KeplerA11ySettingsInterfaceTurbo, and VoiceView labels on every focusable element
A table in the README separating verified from simulated items, plus friction log entries
hardware: Apple Silicon Mac (M4 Pro, 24 GB) running the Vega Virtual Device, plus 2–3 phones of any brand. An optional Fire TV Stick 4K Select (₹5,499) for a real-device take.

estimate.assumptions: All estimates. hours_duo is per person when split (TV app vs backend and PWA), including about 15% coordination overhead. Includes 14 h for Vega toolchain, Rosetta and VVD setup, 10 h for the demo video and 8 h for submission writing. Assumes a developer fluent in React and TypeScript and new to Vega. Cloud usage assumes about 300 min of audio in dev and demo. Transcribe batch is $0.006–0.024/min (the digest lists $0.006/min at medium confidence; $0.024 is a conservative assumption), so ≤$7.20. Nova Lite at about 2M input and 0.5M output tokens costs about $0.24 (verified rates). WebSocket, Lambda, DynamoDB and S3 are assumed to stay under a few dollars at demo volume (WebSocket pricing not verified).

blockers: WebSocket support on React Native for Vega is documented only through a WebFetch summary. The CommonScene entrant corroborates it, but it needs a day-1 spike.
Rosetta is missing on macOS 27, so the Vega tools will not run until it is installed.
A new AWS account may have Bedrock quota set to 0 (two forum reports, no escalation path).
Demo logistics: at least three consenting real people, plus authentic old photos owned by the team's family.
Phone microphone permission and HTTPS on a local network during development (use a tunnel or deployed endpoints).
fallback: If WebSocket fails on Vega, use HTTP long-polling with fetch at 1 s. If Transcribe latency hurts the live demo, show live captions from the phone's Web Speech API, label them as such, and use Transcribe for the archive. If the Vega toolchain blocks, build Fire OS react-native-tvos and record on a real Fire TV Stick over adb. The Android TV emulator is avoided because the rules name only a device or the Fire TV/Vega simulator.
judge_rejection_risks: It can look like another Jackbox or GameNight QR-join app, and QR pairing is common among entrants.
It may read as 'transcription plus slideshow', and question generation is a latent LLM capability.
Remento already turns photos into prompts, so novelty depends on the group mechanism and conflict tracking.
Impact is emotional rather than functional and is hard to quantify. Potential Impact may score lower than for health or accessibility entries.
Privacy and consent concerns for recordings of older relatives and minors.
The demo depends on staged family footage, so authenticity may be questioned.
risk_profile: Medium-high execution risk: realtime choreography across several devices and a demo with live people. Low TV-platform risk, since the TV only renders, takes D-pad input and plays audio. Medium privacy risk (family voices). Low compute cost.
aws_builder_path: The AWS services do real work: API Gateway WebSocket provides managed fan-out with no server to keep warm through judging; S3 presigned uploads keep media off the TV; Transcribe gives word timestamps for caption sync; Nova Lite generates questions and extracts claims in structured form; DynamoDB stores room state. Optional: a Strands agent ('interviewer') with deterministic tools (list_open_conflicts, unanswered_people) chooses which three questions to propose. Development workflow uses Claude Code on Bedrock or Kiro Crew, which counts per forum 45321. Nova keeps spend within the promotional credits.
open_source_path: Publish 'vega-room-kit' under MIT. It contains: a React Native for Vega hook (useRoom) for QR pairing, presence, roles and reconnect; the phone PWA client; a reference Lambda/WebSocket backend; and a signed join-token spec, with vitest tests and protocol docs. Value: visible entrants (CommonScene, HomeBoard, Cinemastamps) each rebuilt phone pairing, and Amazon's documented Matter Casting route needs a Device Attestation Certificate, which is heavy for small apps. This is a new integration pattern, in line with the rules' Open Source creative example.

conditions: A 2-person split (about 85 h each, the concept's estimate) or a solo scope cut to about 110 h or less. For example, make the multi-teller claim ledger a stretch goal and use labelled Web Speech captions live, with Transcribe only for the archive.
At least 3 consenting participants are available for the shoot, including an elder; minors need guardian consent. Old photos must be genuinely family-owned.
Phone-to-TV events reach the Vega app on the VVD over WSS, or over 1 s polling, by day 2.
Bedrock Nova Lite and Transcribe are usable in us-east-1 on a Paid-plan AWS account (quota is not 0).

For a real-device take: the Vega path needs the 4K Select confirmed on OS 1.2, an Amazon Developer account and a USB data cable. The Fire OS path needs a Fire OS stick or AQC Live Device Interaction. Not adb on the 4K Select.
Do not commit family media to a public repo. Use consented sample media, or a private repo shared with the 6 reviewers plus testing@devpost.com (forum 45418, 45420).
gate.crowding_notes: Storytelling theme: 0 of about 37 visible Fire TV repos (github.md §2; a lower bound). The QR phone-companion pattern is common, though: CommonScene, HomeBoard and Cinemastamps per research claim GH-035. The memory/elder theme has about 15 repos across tracks, including Marc-Dvci/Mantel (a Fire TV 'patient memory' for dementia). Fire TV has about 12 visible repos per prize slot.
gate.day_one_proof: On the VVD (Rosetta installed, Vega SDK 0.24, Node 20 via nvm), a Vega RN app must do four things: receive 50 phone-PWA events over WSS through API Gateway with a median under 500 ms (or work over 1 s polling); show a phone-uploaded JPEG full-screen from a presigned GET; play an S3 audio clip through react-native-w3cmedia with currentTime advancing. Separately, Bedrock Nova Lite in us-east-1 must return a structured claims JSON for one test transcript.
gate.redesign_to_pass: Not a gate fail. To remove the conditions for a solo builder: (a) ship the question relay and episode player first, at about 100 h, and treat the claim ledger as a stretch; (b) drop the adb fallback and stay VVD-only, which is rules-compliant, or use AQC Live Device Interaction with a separate Fire OS build; (c) script the shoot with 3 consenting adults if minors complicate consent.

name: WordGlow TV: adaptive same-language subtitle stories
track: Fire TV (primary). Mini challenges: AWS Builder, Open Source.
pitch: A Vega OS kids' channel of short, original, illustrated stories. Each word lights up on the TV at the moment the narrator says it, using Amazon Polly word speech marks. Pressing Play/Pause freezes on the current word, D-pad left and right move between words, and OK replays just that word's slice of audio. The app logs each replay and how long the child stays paused. These signals make up the household's 'tricky words', which drive the next generated episode: the target words recur, sentences get shorter or longer, and the highlight pace changes for each child profile. It builds on Same Language Subtitling (SLS), a TV literacy method with field evidence in India.
primary_user: Early or struggling readers aged about 5–9, watching with a parent or grandparent. First segment: English-medium learners in Indian households. Second: US households. Profiles live on the device.
original_mechanism: (1) Word clock from speech marks. Polly returns word marks (time, start, end, value) alongside the MP3. The TV binary-searches the audio player's currentTime against the marks to find the active word. Replaying a word means seeking to mark[i].time and pausing at mark[i+1].time, with no extra synthesis. (2) Household-adaptive generation behind a deterministic gate. Each child's replay and dwell signals update a difficulty profile. A Strands agent generates the next episode under explicit constraints (target words, maximum sentence length, share of known words). A readability gate written in plain code, not an LLM, rejects drafts and asks for a rewrite until the constraints pass. Only then are Polly and illustration generation called. Episodes are flagged for human review before children see them.
removal_test: Fairly strong, with a stated caveat. The evidence base (SLS) concerns subtitles on TV watched habitually, often with family present. Remove the TV and the product becomes a tablet read-along app, a different and crowded category. That move gives up the habitual viewing slot and co-viewing. Caveat: word highlighting itself works on any screen. The bet that the TV drives more exposure than a tablet has not been tested here.
wow_moment_45s: 0:00 A story plays, and each word glows in sync with the narrator. 0:10 The child presses Play/Pause, and the focus ring lands on 'elephant'. D-pad right moves to 'enormous', OK is pressed, and the narrator says only 'enormous'. 0:20 The parent overlay (Menu) shows 'Tricky words today: enormous, whisper'. 0:30 Pressing 'Next episode' opens a newly generated episode (cached before the demo, and labelled as pre-generated). Its title card reads 'Practice words: enormous ×3', and its sentences are visibly shorter: level 2.0 → 1.5. 0:40 The new episode starts with 'enormous' glowing.

mvp_scope: Vega app on the VVD with three screens: profile picker (PIN-gated parent overlay), episode shelf, and player with word clock
Word-level interaction: pause to focus a word, D-pad to move between words, OK to replay that word's audio slice, with VoiceView labels on each word
Caption font and colors read from KeplerA11ySettingsInterfaceTurbo, with a large-text default
Episode bundle format: mp3, speech-marks JSON, 4 illustrations and metadata, cached in AsyncStorage or on the file system for offline play
Generation pipeline: Strands agent, deterministic readability and target-word gate, Polly MP3 plus word marks, and illustrations, stored in S3 behind CloudFront
Adaptation loop: replay and dwell events sent in batches to the API; the next episode is generated for that profile
8–12 reviewed English episodes across three levels, labelled as AI-generated and human-reviewed
hardware: Apple Silicon Mac with the VVD only. An optional Fire TV Stick 4K Select for a check on real-device timing.

estimate.assumptions: All estimates. hours_duo is per person when split (TV app vs generation pipeline). Includes 14 h for Vega setup, 16 h for writing and reviewing episodes, 10 h for the video and 8 h for submission. Cloud usage assumes about 60 generated drafts and 12 kept episodes of about 1,500 characters each, about 90k characters for Polly. Polly neural pricing was not verified this session; at an assumed $16 per 1M characters that is about $1.50. Nova Lite text costs under $1 (verified rates). Illustrations: about 240 images at an assumed ~$0.04 each (Nova Canvas price not verified) is about $10. S3, CloudFront, Lambda and DynamoDB are assumed near zero at demo volume.

blockers: Precision of audio currentTime and seek on the VVD and Vega devices is unverified. Highlight drift above about 150 ms would undermine the core interaction.
Safety and accuracy of AI-generated children's content. Amazon pulled its own AI Video Recaps after errors (Engadget, 12 Dec 2025).
Consistency of illustrations across pages if Nova Canvas is used. Its availability and price were not verified.
No real children are tested before submission unless parents consent, so efficacy cannot be claimed and only the SLS literature can be cited.
Rosetta and Vega toolchain setup, plus possible Bedrock quota problems.
fallback: If the audio clock jitters on the VVD, run a JS timer started at play() and re-anchor it at each sentence mark. If image generation fails, use simple vector scenes (the react-native-svg Vega port exists). If the generation pipeline is late, ship a hand-reviewed, pre-generated episode set, with adaptation choosing among existing levels instead of generating new ones. If Vega is blocked, use Fire OS on a real stick.
judge_rejection_risks: Could be read as 'a video player with subtitles', which is the rules' 'obvious' example.
AI-generated content for children raises safety concerns, and Amazon has a recent public history of pulled AI recaps.
The SLS evidence covers subtitled songs and films, not AI-generated stories. Judges may see the leap as unproven.
Amazon Kids+ and PBS already serve this audience on Fire TV, which may hurt perceived market need.
An India-first literacy pitch with an English-only MVP could look inconsistent.
There is no outcome data from real children.
risk_profile: Medium. The runtime is a single device with no realtime networking and can play offline from cache, which keeps demo risk low. The core risk is technical: A/V timing precision on Vega is unverified. Reputational and compliance risk around children's content and efficacy claims is high.
aws_builder_path: A multi-service pipeline where each service has a clear job. A Strands agent orchestrates generation with deterministic tools: readability_check, target_word_coverage, synthesize_with_marks (Polly) and illustrate. Bedrock Nova writes drafts, Polly provides audio and word timing (the core sync mechanism), S3 and CloudFront distribute episode bundles, and DynamoDB holds the adaptation signals. This matches the rules' 'Creative' AWS example of a multi-service pipeline plus agent orchestration. Development uses Claude Code on Bedrock or Kiro Crew.
open_source_path: Release 'react-native-word-clock' under MIT: a component and hook that turns Polly speech marks or WebVTT word timestamps into a seek-safe active-word index, slices per-word replay, and renders 10-foot highlighted text with D-pad word focus. It targets RN for Vega, react-native-tvos and web, with vitest unit tests for the binary-search clock and drift correction. Also open a PR adding a speech-mark cue source to the MIT-licensed vega-media-kit. This is a reusable Vega-ready integration pattern, not a README edit.

conditions: Fit solo scope within about 117 h: drop Nova Canvas in favour of react-native-svg scenes, and drop live generation in favour of hand-reviewed pre-generated episodes.
On day 1, the VVD word clock must reach a median error of 150 ms or less with no word highlighted more than 150 ms early, or the JS-timer re-anchoring fallback must meet the same bar.
Differentiation from usv240/everyword must be visible in the first 30 s of the video: per-word D-pad replay plus the household-adaptive next episode. Otherwise Quality of the Idea is at risk.
No efficacy claims about real children. Any child viewing only with parental consent.
AI-generated assets must be licensed into the repo, or the repo made private and shared with the reviewers (forum 45418).
Bedrock Nova Lite access is confirmed in us-east-1 or us-west-2.
gate.crowding_notes: Direct visible collision with usv240/everyword (created 2026-09-14, pushed 2026-10-03, MIT; README read via Firecrawl 2026-10-03, .firecrawl/idea-gate-everyword.md; all of the following are entrant claims, unverified). It has the same Same Language Subtitling thesis on Fire TV, word-by-word highlighting built from Polly speech marks and Transcribe, 'read-that-line-again' and slow mode, the published npm package karaoke-captions-react (which collides with the proposed react-native-word-clock OSS piece), a live MCP server, a Strands agent, 153 tests, and footage filmed on an Amazon-hosted Fire TV. usv240 is a serial, highly polished entrant. Other overlaps: moiz-lakkadkutta/lingo (dual subtitles), samadon1/sightline (caption runtime), vega-media-kit CueOverlay.
gate.day_one_proof: A single-screen Vega app on the VVD plays one Polly neural MP3 through w3cmedia. It logs highlighted-word error against the speech marks over 3 minutes and must show a median of 150 ms or less with zero words lit more than 150 ms early. Play/Pause followed by OK must replay exactly one word's slice. The same day, write a 3-line differentiation against everyword that a judge could verify from the video.
gate.redesign_to_pass: This is not a gate fail, but the headline thesis is already visibly built by a strong entrant. Two options. Option (a): drop the SLS/karaoke framing and pitch only the household-adaptive practice loop (replay and dwell signals, then a tricky-word profile, then a constrained next episode behind a deterministic readability gate) plus per-word D-pad replay; also make the Open Source piece a Vega port of an existing MIT React Native caption library, which matches the rules' own example of 'adding Vega support to a popular React Native library'. Option (b): choose a different concept.

name: BigPrint: a talking TV magnifier where the remote is the shutter
track: Fire TV (primary). Mini challenges: AWS Builder, Open Source.
pitch: For older adults with low vision, a spare phone on a cheap stand becomes the camera and the Fire TV becomes the large display of a video magnifier. They press OK on the remote and the paired phone, running a kiosk page, photographs the letter on the table. Within seconds the TV shows the page reflowed at 60–96 px in the viewer's high-contrast colors and reads it aloud sentence by sentence. It also shows a card answering what this is, who sent it, what they want, by when and how much. Every fact on the card has a 'Show me' action that zooms into the exact region of the photographed page, using Textract geometry, so the user can check it. 'Send to Priya' shares the card with a family helper only after an explicit on-screen confirmation.
primary_user: Adults aged 65 and over with low vision who live independently, plus one remote family helper (often an adult child).
original_mechanism: (1) Remote-as-shutter across devices. A TV key event becomes a WSS command to a paired phone page that keeps a live getUserMedia stream and Wake Lock. The phone grabs a full-resolution still and uploads it, so the older adult never handles the phone. (2) Fact cards grounded in the source. Textract AnalyzeDocument with QUERIES and LAYOUT returns answers with confidence scores and bounding boxes. Nova Lite may only restate facts in plain language using the Textract lines it was given, each with a line ID. Facts below a confidence threshold show as 'Not sure, show me' instead of a value. The TV renders the source crop from the geometry, so every claim can be checked by eye. Account numbers are masked to the last 4 digits on screen.
removal_test: Strong. In the existing CCTV magnifier category, a large display is the whole point, and the TV is that display. Remove the TV and the product becomes a phone magnifier showing a few words at a time on a 6-inch screen, which is the pain point of the category. Honest caveat: cheap magnifiers that plug into a TV also use the TV (a Reddit snippet, not read, mentions $60–80 units). Our difference comes from AI reflow, fact cards grounded in the source and the remote-as-shutter design, not from the TV alone.
wow_moment_45s: 0:00 A phone on a stand points down at an electricity bill on the coffee table. The viewer presses OK on the remote. 0:04 The TV shows 'Electricity bill · Due 12 Oct · ₹2,340' in yellow on black at about 90 px. 0:12 Down then OK on 'Show me': the TV zooms into the photographed bill with a box around the amount. 0:22 Play: the reflowed text is read aloud while the current line is enlarged. 0:35 Menu, 'Send to Priya?', OK: a confirmation appears. Under 45 s.

mvp_scope: Vega app with five screens: pair phone (QR), reading view (reflow with line-stepping), fact card, 'Show me' zoom, share confirmation
Phone kiosk page: camera preview, Wake Lock, capture on WSS command, upload confirmation tone

Backend: API Gateway WebSocket and HTTPS, Lambda, S3 (SSE-KMS, 24 h lifecycle delete), Textract AnalyzeDocument (QUERIES and LAYOUT, synchronous, ≤10 MB JPEG), Nova Lite restatement restricted to cited line IDs
Polly sentence-level read-aloud of the reflowed text (no per-word highlight; a hardware rival already does that)
Confidence threshold logic with 'Not sure, show me' states, and masking of long digit strings
Helper share: card plus crop link sent to a pre-invited helper page after confirmation on the TV
An evaluation script over 30 of the team's own redacted English documents, with field accuracy published in the README
hardware: Apple Silicon Mac with the VVD, one spare phone (Android or iPhone), a $10–15 phone stand and a desk lamp. Optional: a Fire TV Stick 4K Select for a real-device take with the new tactile remote (that remote ships with the US 3rd-gen stick; India availability not verified).

estimate.assumptions: All estimates. hours_duo is per person (TV app vs backend, phone kiosk and evaluation). Includes 14 h for Vega setup, 10 h for the 30-document evaluation, 10 h for the video and 8 h for submission. Cloud usage assumes about 500 pages analyzed in dev, evaluation and demo. Textract QUERIES pricing was not verified this session; an assumed ≤$0.02 per page gives ≤$10. Polly sentence audio about $1–2 (assumed rate). Nova Lite under $1 (verified rates). WebSocket, Lambda, S3, KMS and DynamoDB a few dollars at most (KMS key about $1 per month, assumption).

blockers: Capture quality: glare, focus and skew from a phone on a stand under room lighting may degrade Textract results.
WebSocket support on Vega is unverified (WebFetch summary only).
Language coverage: Indian bills often mix scripts, and Textract's support for Hindi is not verified, so the MVP is English-only.
Liability perception around financial and medical documents. The app must stay read-only and say clearly that it can be wrong.
Crowded accessibility theme on Fire TV (8+ audio-description repos and a 'vision assistant' entrant).
fallback: If the remote-triggered channel fails on Vega, have the phone capture automatically when the page is still for 1.5 s and push results to the TV by polling. If Textract QUERIES accuracy is low, use DetectDocumentText plus Nova Lite with line-ID citations, still showing evidence crops. If Vega is blocked, use Fire OS on a real stick through adb.
judge_rejection_risks: Fire TV accessibility entries are crowded, and judges may lump this in with audio-description projects.
It may be seen as an OCR wrapper if the grounding and the remote-as-shutter are not shown clearly.
It needs a phone, so it is not literally remote-only, and setting up a phone stand may seem unrealistic for the target user.
Sending sensitive documents to the cloud is a privacy concern, made sharper by the 2026 privacy backlash.
Errors in financial or medical readings would carry liability, and demo evidence of safety may feel thin.
The demo may use simulated low vision rather than real users.
risk_profile: Low-medium technical risk: synchronous Textract plus a simple two-device command channel with a fixed phone. High sensitivity to trust, privacy and accuracy, because the documents are financial and medical. High crowding and collision risk among accessibility entries on Fire TV. Demo risk is low, since one person can record it.
aws_builder_path: Textract AnalyzeDocument QUERIES and LAYOUT provide geometry and confidence that make each fact checkable. That is the core safety feature, not decoration. Bedrock Nova Lite is limited to restating Textract lines with citations. Polly reads aloud. API Gateway WebSocket carries the TV-to-phone shutter command. S3 with KMS and a 24 h lifecycle supports the privacy promise, and DynamoDB holds cards. A published evaluation over 30 documents of field accuracy and the 'not sure' rate gives judges a measured technical claim. Development uses Claude Code on Bedrock or Kiro Crew.
open_source_path: Release 'react-native-tv-reader' under MIT: a 10-foot reflow reader for RN for Vega, react-native-tvos and web. It includes D-pad line-stepping, a focus-safe zoom-to-bounding-box viewer that takes normalized geometry (Textract-compatible), VoiceView-friendly labels, caption-style binding through KeplerA11ySettingsInterfaceTurbo with a non-Vega fallback, and jest tests for the geometry math and focus order. This fills a visible gap: no reusable 10-foot document reader exists in the @amazon-devices port list (103 packages checked on npm).

conditions: Textract QUERIES field accuracy of about 90% or better on the team's own phone-on-stand captures under living-room light, which is the concept's own kill threshold.
Demo documents are team-owned and redacted, or synthetic and labelled. Account numbers are masked on screen. Read-only scope only, with no payment or medication advice.
English-only MVP, since Textract support for Hindi was not verified.
For a real-device take: a Vega 4K Select on OS 1.2 via `vega devmode`, or a Fire OS build on a Fire OS stick or AQC Live Device Interaction.
gate.crowding_notes: The accessibility cluster is the most crowded Fire TV theme: about 12 visible blind/low-vision repos across tracks, at least 8 of them Fire TV AI audio description (github.md theme counts). vikrant-29/ai-tv-vision-assistant ('D-pad-first AI vision assistant designed for Fire TV', Fire OS, Flutter) has unknown scope and is a possible overlap. No visible entrant reads physical documents on the TV. The risk is that judges lump it in with the audio-description entries.
gate.day_one_proof: End to end: an OK key press on the VVD sends 'capture' over WSS or polling. The phone kiosk page on a stand grabs a full-resolution still and PUTs it to S3. Textract AnalyzeDocument QUERIES returns sender, amount and due date with bounding boxes for 10 of the team's own redacted bills, with at least 9 of 10 fields correct. The VVD then renders the reflowed card and a zoomed evidence crop at 60–96 px.
gate.redesign_to_pass: Not required. Recommended: open the video with the contrast to Echo Show Visual Input (10-foot reflow, evidence crops a viewer can check, remote-only control), and keep the confidence-threshold 'Not sure, show me' state visible.

strongest_rival.rival: Apple Magnifier for Mac with Accessibility Reader (Reader Mode), using an iPhone on a stand via Continuity Camera / Desk View
strongest_rival.why: Apple announced this on 13 May 2025 and its accessibility features page now describes it in the present tense. It already does BigPrint's core loop for low-vision users, for free and first-party. An iPhone on a stand is the camera (Continuity Camera; documents via Desk View). The large screen is the display. The user captures a frame and Reader Mode turns the text into a custom legible format: font, size, colour and spacing. The text can be read aloud (Speak Screen), and there are audible prompts for framing the document. So the 'phone on a stand + big-screen reflow + read aloud' half of BigPrint is no longer novel. Free phone apps cover the rest: Seeing AI (Document channel with alignment audio cues, plus 'Ask Seeing AI about the contents') and Google Lookout (Documents mode, Q&A on images). Fire TV's own Miracast display mirroring can also put any Android phone magnifier on the TV for $0. That native mirroring is verified on the Amazon help page; whether Vega devices support it is not verified. What remains for BigPrint, and is not verified in any rival: (1) the TV plus remote as the only control surface, with a fixed phone the user never touches; (2) every fact shown with a zoomed crop of where it is printed, plus a confidence gate ('Not sure, show me'); (3) Android/Fire TV households, which cannot use Apple's Mac+iPhone route (inference).

redteam_round1.differentiation_holds:
Narrowly, and only if the thesis moves. The magnifier half (phone on a stand + big-screen reflow + read aloud) collapses against Apple Magnifier for Mac with Accessibility Reader Mode, which is free and first-party and offers capture-frame, custom font/colour/size, framing prompts and Speak Screen. It also collapses against free phone readers (Seeing AI Document channel, Lookout Documents mode) and Fire TV's native Miracast mirroring of any Android magnifier.
The fact-card half ('who sent it, how much, by when') is a latent multimodal-LLM capability. Seeing AI ('Ask about the contents'), Lookout (image Q&A) and, per a third-party review, Alexa+ (document/photo understanding, also on Fire TV) already answer it. Visible entrants do not collide: GitHub searches for fire tv + textract/ocr/magnifier/document reader found 0 repos created after 15 Aug 2026. vikrant-29/ai-tv-vision-assistant describes photos from a bundled offline dataset, reads no documents, and its backend has never been deployed. The rest of the accessibility cluster is audio description plus one large-target TV UI (simple-mode).
What survives, with no rival verified to do it:
- Remote-only capture on the TV, with a fixed phone the user never touches (Apple's route needs a Mac and an iPhone, and the phone apps need hand aiming and touch).
- Every fact is a non-generative extraction (Textract QUERY_RESULT) shown beside a geometry-cropped zoom of the source, with a confidence gate. This directly addresses a reported Alexa+ weakness: a third-party reviewer found its document extraction 'selective' and missing dates (anecdotal).
That is a defensible wedge, but much narrower than the pitch claims. Originality should be scored on the verification loop and the 10-foot remote-only interaction, not on reflow or reading aloud.
redteam_round1.redesign:
Rename and rescope to 'BigPrint Mail Check': one job, checking a single letter or bill on the TV with the remote alone, where every fact can be verified by eye.
(1) Thesis: lead with 'Show me' evidence zoom plus the 'Not sure' gate plus no-touch remote capture. Do not claim reflow or read-aloud as novel; Apple ships them.
(2) Take Bedrock off the critical path. The card is built only from Textract AnalyzeDocument QUERY_RESULT text, Confidence and Geometry, using at most 6 English queries: sender, document type, amount due, due date, requested action, reference number (masked to the last 4 digits). A deterministic sentence template turns these into plain language. Any field below a 90% confidence threshold renders as 'Not sure, show me'; Textract best practices say financial workflows may need thresholds of 90% or higher. This removes hallucination risk, the Bedrock quota-0 risk, and the 'latent LLM' critique. Nova can return later as an optional, clearly labelled 'explain in plain words' button that cites line IDs.
(3) The reflow view uses LAYOUT/LINE blocks with D-pad line-stepping, bound to KeplerA11ySettingsInterfaceTurbo caption styles, plus Polly sentence speech marks.
(4) Phone kiosk: Android Chrome only, using ImageCapture.takePhoto() for full-resolution stills (unsupported on Safari iOS per caniuse). Add a printed placement mat with corner marks and a desk lamp. If fewer than a minimum number of LINE blocks come back, the TV says 'Move the letter into the box', so it never shows a guessed card.
(5) Cut the helper share to a stretch goal. If time allows, add a read-only card link, sent only after an on-TV confirmation.
(6) Command channel: WSS on Vega, with a pre-built HTTPS long-poll fallback.
(7) OSS mini challenge: publish only the focus-safe zoom-to-normalized-bounding-box viewer and the D-pad line stepper for RN for Vega, with jest tests for the geometry and focus order.
(8) Day-2 kill gates. (a) On 10 synthetic or own redacted English documents captured on the stand under lamp light, at least 9 of 10 QUERY fields are correct and no more than 20% fall below the threshold. If this fails, kill, because without verifiable facts this is a weaker Apple Reader Mode on a TV. (b) Measure p50 latency from OK to card, India to us-east-1. If it is over about 10 s, show staged progress (reflow first, card second) and state the real number in the video. (c) The VVD opens a wss connection to API Gateway; if not, switch to long-poll.
(9) Video: as in the demo fix, one unedited timed take on a TV showing the VVD (or a real 4K Select), synthetic labelled documents, a visible 'Not sure' state, no third-party logos, and competitor comparisons kept in the text only.
Re-estimated effort: about 95–100 h solo, leaving about 15–20 h of buffer. This is an estimate.
redteam_round1.feasibility_attack:
(1) The time budget is not credible as written. 115 h of work against about 117 h of capacity leaves about 2 h of buffer for a solo developer building 6 surfaces: the Vega app, the phone kiosk, the helper page, a backend of 8+ AWS services (API GW WebSocket, Lambda, S3+KMS, Textract, Bedrock, Polly, DynamoDB), a 30-document evaluation and an OSS package, plus video, friction log and feedback. Known setup tax adds to this. macOS 27 removed Rosetta. Node is v25 but the samples pin Node 18–20. The VVD crashes when free memory falls below 2 GB on a 24 GB Mac that will also be screen-recording (firetv.md §2–3).
(2) Capture resolution is a hard technical constraint the concept missed. The Textract limits page says the minimum detectable text height is 15 px, which is 8 pt at 150 DPI. A 1080p frame grabbed from getUserMedia gives roughly 92–130 DPI on an A4 page (computed inference), so small print on bills will drop out. A true full-resolution still needs ImageCapture.takePhoto(). caniuse shows it supported on Chrome for Android but not on Safari iOS (through 27.2). The kiosk must therefore be Android Chrome, or request a 4K stream, which is unverified per device.
(3) Character set: the Textract FAQ says it detects the 'Standard English alphabet and ASCII symbols'. The pitch's '₹2,340' likely will not come back as ₹ (inference). If Nova adds the symbol back, the 'verbatim, checkable' claim breaks.
(4) Language: Queries are English-only (verified in the limits doc). That is fine for the MVP, but it weakens the India story.
(5) Vega WebSocket: the RN-for-Vega 0.83 network page now shows a WebSocket section (FC-scrape this session). It is mirrored upstream React Native documentation, and runtime behaviour on the VVD is untested. VoiceView on the VVD rests on one entrant's anecdote.
(6) The Fire OS fallback is not cheap. It means a second react-native-tvos build. AQC Live Device Interaction does not offer the Vega 4K Select (community thread, May 2026). A real Vega take therefore needs a purchased ₹5,499 stick and `vega devmode` (one forum success, one Reddit failure; anecdotal).
(7) Bedrock quota-0 reports on new accounts (2 forum reports) are a day-1 risk. Removing Nova from the critical path eliminates it.
redteam_round1.demo_attack:
(1) The wow timestamp is probably staged. The storyboard shows the card at 0:04 after OK. The real chain from India is: WSS to us-east-1, then the phone shutter, a 3–8 MB JPEG upload over home Wi-Fi, the S3 event, Lambda, synchronous AnalyzeDocument QUERIES+LAYOUT, Nova Lite, Polly, DynamoDB, and the push to the VVD. That plausibly takes about 6–12 s; this is an estimate and has not been measured. A cut at that moment is exactly what a skeptical judge looks for.
(2) The 'TV' in the demo is a Mac window. On a laptop screen the VVD loses the 10-foot, large-display premise that the whole removal test rests on.
(3) Two devices and a document have to be visible together. That needs a second camera and a composite, and those edits again invite 'is this real?'.
(4) The ₹ glyph on the hero card may not survive Textract (FAQ: ASCII symbols).
(5) The users are simulated (teammates wearing low-vision glasses). That is acceptable if labelled, but it weakens Impact.
(6) The 'Send to Priya' ending is the least differentiated beat, since sharing a card is commodity.
What would make the wow real: one unedited take with a visible on-screen elapsed timer, covering OK press → reflowed text → fact card → 'Show me' zoom. Show the honest latency, with a progress state. Then show a deliberately smudged or folded field producing 'Not sure, show me' instead of a guess. Display the VVD full-screen on an actual TV over HDMI, captioned 'Vega Virtual Device', or use a real 4K Select. Picture-in-picture a fixed camera on the phone and the document. Use a synthetic USD (or 'Rs.') bill labelled 'synthetic sample'.
redteam_round1.eligibility_attack:
No hard blocker under the Official Rules.
(1) Fire TV rule (Rules L296/L341): the project must run on Fire OS or Vega OS, and the video must show it on a real Fire TV or the Fire TV/Vega simulator. A Vega app on the VVD satisfies this. The phone is an auxiliary sensor and nothing prohibits it. However, the video must show the Vega app doing the work, not just the phone.
(2) Video trademark clause (Rules: 'must not include third party trademarks ... unless the Entrant has permission'): a real electricity bill carries a utility's name and logo, and a comparison slide showing Apple, Seeing AI or Lookout UI or logos is also risky. Use only synthetic, labelled bills with invented sender names. Keep competitor comparisons in the text description, without logos.
(3) Testing clause: the project must be free and unrestricted for judges until judging ends. Keep the AWS backend live through 20 Nov. Add a judge path that needs no stand, such as 'upload a sample image' on the phone page plus bundled sample documents, because judges are unlikely to have the stand setup.
(4) The proprietary-hardware clause (L391) is not triggered, since a phone and a Fire TV are widely available.
(5) India is not an excluded country (rules L238 list).
(6) The organizer's 'latent LLM capability scores poorly' remark (forum 45397) was about Alexa+. The same logic would plausibly hit Quality of the Idea here, because 'what is this bill, how much, when due' is single-turn vision Q&A. Seeing AI, Lookout, and Alexa+ ('document and photo understanding', per a third-party review) already do it. This is a scoring risk, not an eligibility failure.

evidence_checked.finding: Apple press release, 13 May 2025: Magnifier for Mac works with Continuity Camera on iPhone and USB cameras, 'supports reading documents using Desk View', and is integrated with Accessibility Reader, which 'transforms text from the physical world into a custom legible format' (font, colour, spacing, Spoken Content). Saved in .firecrawl/idea-redteam-ftv3-apple-magnifier-mac.json.

Apple features page describes Reader Mode in the present tense: capture a frame of text; adjust font, size and colour; get audible guidance on framing and perspective; read aloud with Speak Screen or Speak Selection. Magnifier for Mac is listed as an 'Update'.

Seeing AI is free. Its Document channel uses alignment audio cues to capture a printed page, and users can 'Ask Seeing AI about the contents'. One user review mentions using it to spot-check mail. Saved in .firecrawl/idea-redteam-ftv3-phone-doc-readers.json.
Google Lookout is free. Documents mode captures a whole page in 30+ languages, Text mode is pitched for 'sorting mail', and Images mode offers Q&A (English only).

Echo Show vision accessibility includes Show and Tell (identify held items) and Alexa+ Visual Input (identify objects, assist with daily tasks). Reading letters or bills is not stated. Saved in .firecrawl/idea-gate-echo-vision-a11y.md.

Third-party review (anecdotal): Alexa+ adds 'document and photo understanding' and reaches Fire TV. Document extraction was 'selective', missing dates. This supports the grounding wedge but also shows an Amazon-native Q&A path exists.

Fire TV natively supports display mirroring from Miracast Android devices (Settings > Display & Sounds > Enable Display Mirroring); iOS and macOS are not supported. Support on Vega devices is not verified. This means a $0 phone-magnifier-on-TV substitute exists.
Query detection is English-only. Minimum detectable text height is 15 px (8 pt at 150 DPI). Up to 15 queries per page synchronously. Images must be 10,000 px or less per side.
Textract detects printed text and handwriting from the 'Standard English alphabet and ASCII symbols', so the ₹ in the demo storyboard is at risk. Queries are English only.
Recommends images of at least 150 DPI, and says workflows involving financial decisions might need confidence thresholds of 90% or higher. Supports the confidence-gate design.
ImageCapture (takePhoto) is not supported on Safari iOS through 27.2 and is supported on Chrome for Android. Full-resolution kiosk stills therefore need Android Chrome.

The RN-for-Vega 0.83 network page includes a WebSocket section (FC-scrape, .firecrawl/idea-judge-vega-network.md). It is mirrored upstream React Native documentation, and runtime behaviour on the VVD is not verified.

The README says it describes images from a bundled offline demo dataset. Its Bedrock backend has 'never been deployed or executed'. It runs on Fire OS via Flutter and does no physical-document capture, so collision is low.

Searches for repos created after 15 Aug 2026: 'fire tv textract', 'fire tv ocr', 'fire tv magnifier' and 'fire tv document reader' returned 0. 'fire tv accessibility' returned 10, mostly audio description, plus rogerkorantenng/simple-mode (large-target TV UI) and Mantel (dementia). None reads documents. The unauthenticated rate limit was hit after 14 queries, so coverage is incomplete.
Forum snippet: the Fire TV Stick Select (Vega) is not available in AQC Live Device Interaction. A real-device Vega take therefore needs a purchased stick.

Fire TV: the project must run on Fire OS or Vega OS, and the video must show it on a device or the Fire TV/Vega simulator (L341). The video must not include third-party trademarks without permission. Judges must have free testing access until judging ends. India is not excluded.

name: CarpoolMend: cross-family carpool driver-gap repair
pitch: When a parent drops a carpool turn, CarpoolMend filters drivers who cannot actually cover it (seats, boosters, arrival window), ranks the rest by a fairness ledger, asks ONE family at a time to accept, and only after acceptance writes every family's calendar with idempotent, compensable writes.
primary_user: Parents in recurring 3-6 family school/sports carpools (US-first; India school/tuition runs plausible - inference).
original_mechanism: Deterministic constraint filter (seat and booster counts, arrive-by with travel time, licensed adult, family availability) + drive-credit fairness ledger + sequential targeted offers implemented as Step Functions .waitForTaskToken tasks with timeout falling through to next candidate + saga writes using client-chosen event IDs so retries are idempotent and compensation is exact + per-family tenant isolation (other families see only time, kids, pickup point).
removal_test: Honest: the engine is host-agnostic. Without Alexa+ it is a smarter GoKid (constraint-ranked targeted offers instead of broadcast). Alexa+ adds the ambient trigger and hands-free acceptance, not the core value. Weakness flagged; fit rests on voice-first household entry, not exclusivity.
wow_moment_45s: Two simulated Echo Shows side by side. Parent A: 'I can't do Thursday hockey pickup.' Card ranks 3 candidates with reasons (Lee: 2 free seats, has booster, owed 1 drive; Patel excluded: car full). Only Lee's screen chimes; Lee says 'Yes, I'll take it.' Both calendars update; audit strip shows 4 writes with idempotency keys. A forced calendar failure on one family visibly triggers compensation and retry.

name: RideBook Access: paratransit trip booking add-on, built to Alexa+ certification requirements
track: Alexa+ (primary); Open Source (mini) via conformance harness; AWS Builder optional
pitch: An add-on a transit agency could publish so ADA paratransit riders book, change and cancel trips by voice instead of waiting on hold. It implements Amazon's published Functional Requirements literally: read-back confirmation, fare breakdown, receipts, duplicate-trip prevention, linked return-trip protection, resumable booking and stable IDs.
primary_user: ADA paratransit riders (people with disabilities incl. blind/low-vision, older adults) and caregivers booking for them; the publisher is the agency (fictional 'Lakeshore Access Transit' in the demo).
original_mechanism: Agency policy-as-config (horizon, negotiation window, pickup window, cancel cutoff, no-show points, fares) compiled from published agency rules; offer holds with TTL and stable chained IDs (search_id -> offer_id -> trip_id); idempotency keys and duplicate/overlap detection; linked-trip graph that prompts for orphaned return legs; resumable booking draft; voice-only renderer enforcing 5-option limit; plus an OSS harness that tests Functional Requirements sections 8 and 13 and emits a report shaped like the Local Inspector's documented certification-verdict.json.
removal_test: Without Alexa+ the same MCP server could back a phone IVR or a ChatGPT app, and agencies already have apps (Via, TripCheck). Book it?' 'Yes.' Receipt card. Rider says 'book it' again -> 'You already have trip LAT-4821.' Later: 'Cancel my morning ride' -> 'That is on time. Your 1:30 return is still booked - cancel it too?'

strongest_rival.rival: Spare AI Voice. Ecolane IVA and TripMaster IVA offer the same thing on other scheduling platforms.
strongest_rival.why: Spare's product page says AI Voice answers rider calls, books trips, cancels rides and makes changes inside the agency's own scheduling system, so riders do not wait on hold. Listed use cases include after-hours booking, caregiver trip confirmation, paratransit ETA checks and multilingual voice plus SMS ('No new apps to download'). The product is shipping, not a concept. Metro Magazine (31 May 2024) names MVTA, Auburn, Milton and CapMetro as implementing it. PSTA's official press release (27 Aug 2025) says ADA paratransit (Access) riders can book, check status and cancel without waiting on hold, and that the system remembers favourite locations and payment methods (a $134k contract). Ecolane IVA (and TripMaster IVA) offers the same: 24/7, 30+ languages, and the example utterance 'Cancel my 3pm return trip', with a Via Mobility pilot. That is ALX-2's headline value ('book, change and cancel trips by voice instead of waiting on hold'), already delivered with real scheduler integration. It also runs on a phone every rider already owns, with no Echo, no Alexa+ subscription and no US-only add-on. The concept's rival table lists only apps, TripCheck and Uber, and misses this whole category.

redteam_round1.differentiation_holds:
No.
(1) Voice booking, changes and cancellations without hold time: already shipped by Spare AI Voice (2024-, PSTA 2025), Ecolane IVA and TripMaster IVA, all integrated with real schedulers and available 24/7. DREDF also notes that some agencies already take bookings through IVR.
(2) Self-service booking: already offered by myRTCpara (book, check, cancel, track), the Via-powered Alexandria DOT app (one-time and round trips, edit or cancel until 4:30pm the day before), MATBUS, STA PassApp and RTS Plus.
(3) Voice ride booking on Alexa+: native through Uber, and ride booking is a partner-gated Category SDK category.
(4) Read-back, explicit yes, fare breakdown, receipts, duplicate prevention, stable IDs, max 5 options: these are certification table stakes every transactional add-on must meet (FR §8, §9, §13), not originality.

The residual delta is narrow:
- The Echo channel for paratransit. No existing Alexa paratransit-booking skill surfaced in two searches, which is a weak negative.
- A linked-leg orphan prompt and late-cancel policy disclosure. These are small UX features; whether the vendor agents already do them is unverified. Ecolane's own example handles 'cancel my 3pm return trip'.
- An OSS harness adjacent to mcp-voice-simulator and everyword.

Crowding is genuinely low: a GitHub search for paratransit repos created after 31 Aug returned 2 repos, neither of them Alexa+. But being uncrowded is not the same as being differentiated.
redteam_round1.redesign:
Not recommended as the primary-track thesis. No narrower paratransit framing restores originality.
- Caregiver confirmation is already in Spare.
- Arrival call-outs and texts already exist: Access LA call-outs and Pace TripCheck imminent-arrival alerts.
- Rider-side no-show protection needs agency data the add-on cannot have.
- 'Alexa+ channel adapter for an agency's existing scheduler' is the rules' Obvious wrapper.

Salvage one component: the conformance harness as the Open Source mini contribution, attached to whichever primary project is chosen. Specify it as follows:
- A separate MIT repo, e.g. 'addon-fr-checks'.
- A CLI that connects to any MCP server over Streamable HTTP, negotiating 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18 and 2025-11-25.
- It replays scripted lifecycles: create, modify one parameter, status, duplicate attempt, cancel without confirmation, interrupted purchase then resume, and invalid parameters.
- It asserts about 12 machine-checkable rules from FR §8 and §13: every tools/list entry is invocable; inputSchema is valid and enforced; isError is used rather than malformed payloads; IDs chain from search to details to book; duplicate requests return the existing ID; destructive tools refuse without a confirmation token; the charged amount equals the quoted amount; no tool names, JSON or internal IDs appear in customer-facing text.
- It emits its own JSON schema with PASS/WARN/FAIL values, not the gated certification-verdict.json shape or 'CERTIFIED' strings, with the banner 'unofficial; not Amazon certification'.
- It includes tests and a tiny reference server.
The §9 voice-only rules (max 5 options, read-back) can be checked only heuristically against the text content, so label those checks WARN-only.
redteam_round1.feasibility_attack:
Feasible for a solo developer in 20 days. There is no blocker, but the 88 h estimate hides several sinks.
(a) Sessionful 2025-11-25 Streamable HTTP on Lambda + API Gateway (inference): SSE streams and server-to-client elicitation fit poorly there (API Gateway integration timeouts, no streaming on HTTP API). Plan for JSON-response mode with no elicitation and all state in DynamoDB, which also removes the 'MCP elicitation' line from the pitch.
(b) Cognito as the OAuth 2.1 server: you must serve RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata yourself, and Cognito has no Dynamic Client Registration, so the simulated host has to be pre-registered. That is roughly 6-10 h (estimate) for a flow judges never see. Swap it for a labelled, pre-linked test rider.
(c) The simulated host's language understanding is the trap. A deterministic grammar is allowed, but it makes 'arrive by 10 ... 10 is full ... I'll take 9:35' brittle and visibly scripted. An LLM host adds about 6-10 h (estimate) and Bedrock new-account quota risk (two forum reports of quota 0).
(d) Sending receipts through the SES sandbox requires verified recipients. That is fine for a test inbox.
(e) The 24 h harness is the first thing to cut if time runs short.
(f) An India-based developer with no paratransit contacts can only seed configs from public pages. The falsification test's 'one screen-reader user' is achievable remotely, but no real agency or rider validation is possible.
Net: buildable with about 20-30 h buffer if OAuth and the Echo Show carousel are trimmed (estimate).
redteam_round1.demo_attack:
The 45 s wow is a scripted multi-turn booking against a mock scheduler whose '10 is full' is a seeded capacity value. Judges see hotel and restaurant booking flows constantly. The two non-trivial beats, the duplicate catch ('You already have trip LAT-4821') and the orphaned-return-leg prompt, last about 10 s and look like ordinary chatbot replies unless the video exposes the conditional write or trip graph. Even then they read as backend hygiene, not a new capability.

The voice-only 'Echo Dot' runs in a browser: a mic or text box plus TTS. That is credible, but it is not a wow. With a fictional agency and no riders, every impact statement is hypothetical.

A judge or AI-assisted reviewer who knows Spare or Ecolane will see an existing product category, already deployed at real agencies, rebuilt with a mock. Their public pages even host call recordings of trip booking.

Latent-LLM test:
- The conversational layer (intent parsing, slot filling, read-back phrasing, the 'cancel my morning ride' resolution) is exactly what Alexa+ and the vendors' LLM agents already do.
- The non-latent part (booking horizon, negotiation window, cancel cutoff, no-show points, idempotency) belongs, in any real deployment, to the agency's scheduler (Spare, Ecolane, Trapeze, Via).
- A real add-on would therefore shrink to an MCP layer over that scheduler's API. That is the rules' L443 'Obvious: basic MCP wrapper around an existing API', with the mock policy engine as duplicated logic.
redteam_round1.eligibility_attack:
There is no hard rules blocker. Rules L298 and L343 accept a self-hosted MCP server (2025-11-25 or later) over Streamable HTTP, or a simulated Alexa+ experience 'built using any AI or agentic tool'. The repo must include the simulation source and the video must clearly show the simulation. Forum 45058 also allows deterministic runtime rules. Remaining eligibility risks:
(1) The OSS harness copies the schema of Amazon's gated certification-verdict.json, including the verdict values CERTIFIED/CONDITIONAL/NOT_CERTIFIED (Local Inspector doc). That can read as claiming an Amazon certification outcome. Use a different file name and schema with PASS/WARN/FAIL only, and add an 'unofficial' banner.
(2) The pitch says it implements Amazon's Functional Requirements 'literally', including 'linked return-trip protection'. The FR page (last updated 21 Jul 2026) has duplicate prevention, resumable purchase, read-back and policy/fee disclosure before cancel, but no linked-trip requirement. Presenting your own feature as an Amazon requirement invites a 'misleading claims' critique.
(3) Amazon's add-ons home lists ride booking as a partner-only Category SDK category. That does not make the entry ineligible, but it signals that Amazon treats ride booking as partner (Uber) territory.
(4) The hosted endpoint must stay live through 20 Nov (forum 45411), or the project must ship a local-run path.
(5) Real agency names may appear only as cited config sources, never as branding.
(6) The OSS mini needs a separately licensed repo or contribution; per forum 45310 that is fine.

name: Said & Done: a two-key promise board for households (Bee + Fire TV)
track: Bee (primary). The Fire TV (Vega) app is a secondary surface. Multi-track judging is allowed, but a project can win only one track prize.
pitch: Promises spoken at home are captured by Bee and become proposals that carry the verbatim quote. The other person accepts or declines on the living-room Fire TV. Any later change must be accepted again, and an item closes only when the counterparty confirms it is done. This is accepted ownership, not another to-do list.
primary_user: Two-adult households where one adult wears Bee and the other does not, for example working parents splitting school, medical and home logistics. The non-wearer acts through the shared Fire TV with no app to install. Assumption: the household has a Fire TV; the demo may use the Vega Virtual Device instead.
original_mechanism: A two-key commitment ledger. Each spoken promise becomes a record with an evidence pointer: Bee conversation_uuid, utterance text, speaker label and conversation start_time. Every state transition needs a different party for each key. The speaker proposes and the counterparty accepts; later, the owner claims done and the counterparty confirms. DynamoDB conditional writes enforce this, so a double accept or a self-accept is impossible. A later utterance is linked as a revision by matching counterpart plus semantic similarity, and it reopens the acceptance gate. Privacy is enforced by construction: speakers not mapped to a household member (guests) are dropped before storage, quotes on unaccepted items expire via TTL after 72 h, and a decline deletes the quote. Only wearer-owned accepted items are mirrored to Bee todos with alarm_at, and their completion is read back through `bee changed`, because the stream reportedly does not deliver todo events.
removal_test: Without Bee, the product becomes a manually typed shared board, which is Cozi, Hearth and Caring Village territory. The core is lost: automatic capture of spoken promises with verbatim evidence, and revision linking. So Bee is indispensable. Without Fire TV, the board still works as a phone web page. Fire TV is a surface choice: it reaches the non-wearer without an install and matches the organizers' cross-device example, but it is not indispensable. Weakness: Bee already extracts the wearer's commitments natively. Our value rests entirely on the second key (acceptance), the revision chain and confirmed close-out. Their absence in rivals is unverified, not proven.
wow_moment_45s: On camera (consenting adults), the partner asks: 'Can you book Riya's dentist appointment before Friday? Her tooth is still bothering her.' The wearer replies at length, ending with 'I'll call them tomorrow morning' (well over 50 words). A cut with an on-screen clock shows the real processing delay. The Fire TV board (VVD or a Fire TV Stick) shows a new Proposed card: 'Arjun to Meera: book dentist before Fri', with the quote and time. The partner presses Select > Accept. The card moves to Accepted, and on the wearer's iPhone the Bee app shows a new todo with a Thursday 9:00 alarm. Second beat: the wearer later says 'they only had Monday', and the card turns amber: 'Changed, needs Meera's OK'.

rivals.our_difference: Acceptance by the counterparty, revisions that must be re-accepted, counterparty-confirmed completion, and a shared TV surface for the non-wearer.

rivals.name: Otter (My Action Items)
rivals.our_difference: Household rather than meeting context, ambient wearable capture rather than a meeting bot, and explicit counterparty acceptance and close-out.

rivals.name: Hearth Display / Hearth Helper

rivals.name: Caring Village
rivals.our_difference: Spoken capture, evidence pointers and revision linking. Claiming in Caring Village overlaps with our acceptance step, so acceptance alone is not novel.

rivals.name: Alexa+ household features
rivals.our_difference: Commitments come from ambient Bee capture rather than being set by voice or app, and they need two-party acceptance.

mvp_scope: Local ingestion daemon on the Mac: `bee stream --json` for liveness plus `bee changed --cursor` every 60 s as the completeness backstop, with the cursor persisted only after processing, utterance dedupe (issue #3), and fixture replay for tests labelled SIMULATED.
One-time household setup: map Bee speaker labels to 2 named members. Unmapped speakers are dropped before any model call.
Commitment extraction (Bedrock) producing an evidence pointer: conversation_uuid, a quote of 25 words or fewer, start_time, proposer and owner.

Two-key state machine (proposed, accepted or declined, revision-proposed, re-accepted, done-claimed, done-confirmed) behind API Gateway, Lambda and DynamoDB conditional writes, with unit tests on every transition.
Fire TV Vega app: a four-column board (Proposed / Accepted / Changed / Done), D-pad focus handling, Accept, Decline and Confirm-done, and pairing by a 6-digit code.
Bee write-back: a wearer-owned accepted item becomes `bee todos create --alarm-at`; completion is detected via `bee changed`.
Revision linking: a later utterance by the same counterpart that semantically matches an open item becomes a 'Changed' card that needs re-acceptance.
Consent and purge: a first-run household consent screen on the TV, a 72 h TTL on unaccepted quotes, and decline deletes the quote.
hardware: Required: a Bee Pioneer ($49.99, ships only to the US) paired with an iPhone running the Bee iOS app (iOS 17.6+), or an iPhone plus an Apple Watch (watchOS 10+) running Bee. Watch ambient-capture parity with Pioneer is unverified, though a forum participant reports the Watch works as a recording source. Android is not viable from India (the app is US-only and a pairing block is reported). An Apple-silicon Mac runs the Bee CLI and the Vega Virtual Device (Vega tools need about 20 GB of disk; 48 GB is free). Optional: a Fire TV Stick 4K Select (Rs 5,499, Vega OS) for real-device footage. People: a second consenting adult on camera.

Claude Haiku 4.5 revision and owner linking: 600 calls x (5k in + 400 out), about $4.20. Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB and CloudWatch at demo volume: about $0-5, mostly free tier. Developer Mode unlock failed for at least one iOS user, and `bee login` with the post-23-Sep-2026 Amazon-account sign-in is undocumented.

Household coordination is a saturated theme (Alexa+ family calendar and Visual ID reminders, Skylight Assistant, Hearth, Cozi, Fambot).

name: Explain-Back: on-wrist retrieval coaching from your own tutoring sessions
track: Bee (primary). Education priority use case; matches the organizers' 'on-wrist coaching for learning' and 'Agent Skills' examples.
pitch: After a tutoring session or consented lecture captured by Bee, Explain-Back schedules spaced 'explain it back in a minute' prompts as Bee todos. The student answers aloud with the Bee button, and an Agent Skill grades the spoken explanation against the tutor's exact words. It shows what was covered, what was missed and any misconception, then writes mastery back to Bee as facts and books the next targeted prompt.
primary_user: University or college students, and self-learners preparing for exams, who attend 1:1 or small-group tutoring, office hours, or lectures where the instructor consents to recording. The student is the Bee wearer. Answers are given alone, so answer capture has no bystanders.
original_mechanism: An evidence-anchored explain-back loop. (1) A speaker allow-list (tutor plus student, chosen once per session) drops everyone else's utterances before any model call. (2) A rubric of key ideas is built for each session, each idea anchored to verbatim tutor utterances with timestamps. (3) Prompts always ask for a roughly one-minute explanation, so answers clear Bee's ~50-word processing threshold; the platform constraint becomes pedagogy (elaborative retrieval). (4) Prompts are released as Bee todos with alarm_at by a context gate: no active conversation in `bee now` or the stream in the last 5 minutes, and the student is preferably at a 'study' location cluster. (5) The answer arrives as a Bee voice note (`journal-created` / `journal-text`) and is linked to the open prompt. A grader returns covered, missing and misconception, each with side-by-side quotes from the tutor and the student. (6) Leitner intervals (1, 3, 7 days); a miss spawns a prompt aimed at the missing idea, and mastery is written back with `bee facts create`.
removal_test: Without Bee, a student could record with a phone into RemNote, Studr or StudyFetch and type answers. The 'session to questions' half survives unchanged; that part is commodity. What dies is the Bee-dependent loop: hands-free spoken explain-back answers in the same data store as the source session, the context gate (no prompts during a live conversation), and mastery written back into Bee facts. So Bee is indispensable to the explain-back loop but not to question generation. We deliberately cut any flashcard UI so the product is the Bee-dependent loop. Flagged weakness: if voice-note answers cannot be captured reliably (the 50-word threshold, latency, the Watch path), the product degrades into a clone of the rivals.
wow_moment_45s: The student's phone (and wrist, if mirroring works) shows the Bee todo 'Explain-Back #4: why doesn't a catalyst change the equilibrium constant? Answer aloud, about 1 minute.' The student presses the Bee button and explains for about 70 words, including one plausible misconception. Seconds to minutes later (the real delay is shown with a clock), the dashboard shows 2 key ideas in green, 1 missing idea in grey, and the misconception in red, next to the tutor's exact quote and timestamp from yesterday's session. In the Bee app, the todo is completed, a targeted follow-up todo appears for tomorrow 8:00, and a new fact appears: 'Can explain: catalysts and equilibrium (mastered 2026-10-14)'.

rivals.name: RemNote

name: TriedThat: spoken debugging memory that stops coding agents repeating your dead ends
track: Bee (primary). Developer-experience priority use case; candidate for AWS Builder (Claude Code on Bedrock) and Open Source mini-challenges.
pitch: While you debug aloud or pair, Bee hears 'I bumped the timeout to 30 seconds and it still flakes'. TriedThat turns that narration into symbol-linked attempt records. When you hand the bug to Claude Code, hooks inject what you already ruled out, with your exact words. If the agent starts editing toward a ruled-out fix, TriedThat stops and asks. The pull request gets a cited 'ruled out during debugging' section only after you tick a Bee todo.
primary_user: Individual developers and pairs who debug aloud or pair-program and then hand work to coding agents (Claude Code, Kiro). Solo narration mode has no bystanders. Pair mode requires the partner's opt-in.
original_mechanism: A symbol-grounded attempt ledger with a deterministic collision guard. (1) A spoken-identifier aligner maps transcribed tokens to the repo's symbol table (tree-sitter or ctags index; camel/snake splitting; phonetic plus edit-distance match), so 'retry with back off' resolves to retryWithBackoff() in src/net/retry.ts. (2) An extractor turns narration windows into attempt records: hypothesis, action, outcome, verdict (ruled-out, confirmed or unknown), symbols, quotes, and Bee conversation id and timestamps. (3) Claude Code hooks: UserPromptSubmit adds matching ruled-out attempts as additionalContext. PreToolUse on Edit, Write and Bash scores the proposed change against ruled-out attempts (symbol overlap plus text similarity) and returns permissionDecision 'ask' with the quote as the reason. (4) The PR provenance section is appended only after the developer ticks a Bee todo ('Share 2 debugging notes in PR #42?'), detected via the changefeed.
removal_test: Without Bee, developers would have to type what they tried mid-debug, which in practice they rarely do (assumption), so the product has no input. Bee is indispensable as the source. The harder test is removing our layer instead: Bee MCP plus Claude Code already lets an agent search transcripts. If that baseline avoids repeated dead ends as well as TriedThat, our product is a thin wrapper and Bee alone delivers the value. The falsification test is built around exactly this baseline.
wow_moment_45s: Split screen. Left: the developer, wearing Bee, debugging a flaky checkout test aloud: 'I bumped the timeout to 30 seconds and it still fails, so it's not timing. I also flushed Redis, no change...' (60+ words). Right: the terminal runs `claude "fix the flaky checkout test"` twice on the same commit. Run 1 (no TriedThat): the agent's first edit raises TIMEOUT_MS. Run 2 (TriedThat): the first message shows 'Ruled out by you at 14:02 (Bee conversation 6531525): timeout to 30s, Redis flush', with quotes, and the agent investigates clock skew instead. When it later tries to edit TIMEOUT_MS, a PreToolUse prompt appears: 'Matches a ruled-out attempt (quote). Proceed?'

rivals.our_difference: Debugging attempts and outcomes rather than decisions or commitments; injected into the coding agent at handoff, with a collision guard rather than filed as documents.

rivals.name: ringfence (hackathon entrant, harshpuri84)
rivals.our_difference: A pull model: the agent is started by the developer, and TriedThat supplies negative knowledge (what was ruled out) plus a deterministic edit-time guard, rather than starting agents from speech.

rivals.name: Mental-Model-Drift (hackathon entrant)
rivals.our_difference: Checks agent actions against the developer's ruled-out attempts, not beliefs against production state.

rivals.name: Bee MCP connected to Claude Code (native baseline)
rivals.our_difference: Structured, symbol-linked attempt records and hooks that inject context and block repeats deterministically, rather than relying on the agent choosing to search.

rivals.name: Granola (MCP connector)
rivals.our_difference: Ambient capture of informal debugging talk (not scheduled meetings) and code-symbol grounding.

mvp_scope: Capture daemon: `bee stream --json` plus `bee changed --cursor`, restricted to sessions the developer tags as debug. Speaker allow-list: the wearer, plus a pair partner only with opt-in.
Repo symbol index (tree-sitter or ctags) and a spoken-identifier aligner with unit tests on at least 30 spoken identifiers.
Attempt extractor producing records with verdicts and evidence pointers, plus a small human-labelled evaluation.
Own MCP server (spec 2025-11-25, stdio and local Streamable HTTP) with tools find_attempts, get_attempt and mark_attempt, plus an Agent Skill describing when to call them.
Claude Code hooks: UserPromptSubmit injects context; PreToolUse on Edit|Write|Bash returns 'ask' with a quote on collision.
PR provenance: append a cited section on `gh pr create` only after a Bee todo tick (read via `bee changed`).
A/B harness: 5 seeded bugs x 3 conditions (no Bee / Bee MCP baseline / TriedThat) x 3 repeats, with logs committed.
hardware: A Bee Pioneer ($49.99, US shipping only) or an iPhone plus Apple Watch (watchOS 10+) running Bee, with an iPhone running the Bee iOS app. A Mac with the target repo, the Bee CLI and Claude Code. No TV, Echo or second person needed in solo mode.

estimate.cloud_cost_usd: Estimate: about $30-60. Extraction with Claude Haiku 4.5: 1,500 windows x (3k in + 400 out), about $7.50. A/B harness: 45 coding-agent runs (5 bugs x 3 conditions x 3 repeats) at an assumed 250k input + 15k output tokens each on Claude Sonnet 5.5 via Bedrock ($2/$10 per M), about $29; prompt caching would lower this, and run size is an assumption. Stretch AgentCore Runtime at about $0.0067 per session (vendor example), under $5. Prices are from the Bedrock and AgentCore pricing pages.
estimate.assumptions: Estimates, not measurements. Solo is about 6.5 focused h/day over 18 working days (about 117 h available), so it fits with about 9 h buffer. Breakdown in hours: setup 5; ingestion 8; symbol index, aligner and tests 16; attempt extraction and labelled evaluation 14; MCP server and Skill 10; Claude Code hooks 8; collision scoring 8; PR provenance and Bee todo consent 6; timeline view 6; A/B harness 10; real narration sessions 5; video, README and friction log 12. hours_duo is hours per person when split (one on aligner, extractor and evaluation, one on MCP, hooks, PR and demo), including about 15% coordination overhead.

Behavioural adoption: many developers do not talk aloud while debugging, so the demo must not look staged and the target user must be framed narrowly.
Transcription of code identifiers may be poor, which is assumed and is why the aligner exists; if alignment fails, the guard is noisy.
Workplace recording policies and teammates' consent for pair mode.
Crowding: kept, ringfence and Mental-Model-Drift already target Bee plus developer workflow.
Bee MCP protocol version (2024-11-05) and stream quirks (43 h drop, missing todo events) need workarounds.

If identifier alignment is weak, prompt the developer to say file names (easier fuzzy matching) and retrieve by time window around commit timestamps. If hook APIs change, fall back to an Agent Skill plus MCP tool the agent calls voluntarily, which is less deterministic and must be stated as such.
judge_rejection_risks: Originality discount: at least 3 visible Bee entrants already target developer workflows, and ringfence is mature and evidence-heavy.
May be judged niche: debugging aloud is uncommon behaviour.
A terminal-heavy demo scores weaker on the Design criterion.
If the A/B delta over `bee mcp connect claude-code` is small, judges will see a wrapper.
Workplace privacy concerns about always-on recording at work.

Technical risk is concentrated in identifier alignment and collision scoring. Highest originality risk among visible Bee entrants. Impact must be proven with an A/B against the native Bee MCP baseline rather than asserted.

The value-adding AWS piece is a stretch goal: host the derived attempt store as an MCP server on AgentCore Runtime with AgentCore Identity, so a teammate's agent on another machine can consult 'what has been ruled out on this bug' without any transcript leaving the wearer's Mac. AgentCore Observability traces show which attempts were injected or blocked. Bedrock model costs for the A/B are reported in the README.

It is reusable by any voice-coding or meeting-to-code tool. Also publish the Claude Code hook pack and Agent Skill under MIT. Candidate upstream: reproduce and document the stream todo-event gap for bee-cli, if confirmed.

Narration sessions exceed 50 words. Pair mode only with the partner's opt-in.
